title: Prune redundant tenant FKs and optimize hot read paths in control-plane DB
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Background: During the tenant-model consolidation in 2023 we introduced duplicate tenant/project identifier columns and multiple foreign-key constraints across several control-plane tables (deployments, routes, credentials). Over time those redundant FKs and lightly-used composite indexes have caused bloat, slow plans for multi-join queries, and long VACUUM/ANALYZE windows. This ticket aims to safely remove the redundant columns/FKs, introduce narrower partial/composite indexes for hot-read access patterns, and land a zero-downtime migration path that keeps referential integrity and minimizes IO and lock contention.

Goals: 
- Remove duplicated tenant_id columns and obsolete FK constraints from 3 high-cardinality tables without downtime.
- Add targeted composite and partial indexes to optimize the 95th-percentile latency for our top 5 control-plane queries (route resolution, tenant metadata lookup, capacity scoring).
- Ensure migrations run with bounded IO, maintainability, and clear rollback steps.
- Update docs and console dashboards to reflect schema changes and new query plans.
acceptance_criteria: All redundant tenant_id columns and FK constraints removed from target tables: deployments, route_mappings, api_keys (after successful validation)
Observed 95th-percentile reduction of control-plane query latency by >=25% for identified hot paths in staging and canary
Migration scripts complete without exclusive locks >15s and without impacting production request latencies beyond the defined canary windows
Data validation queries show 100% referential parity between old and new columns during backfill phase
Runbook and rollback steps validated with DBAs and infra (oncall notified)
plan: Discovery: run table-level statistics, identify FK usage, index size, bloat (pg_stat_user_tables + pg_indexes) - 1 week
Design: decide canonical column names, plan composite/partial indexes that match observed WHERE clauses - 3 days
Pre-migration: create new indexes concurrently (CONCURRENTLY), add computed/views if needed, and prepare backfill jobs - 4 days
Backfill: copy trusted values from legacy columns to canonical column using batched UPDATEs with sleep throttling and progress checkpoints - 4 days
Cutover: switch application read path to prefer canonical column (feature flag) and monitor for anomalies - 2 days
Cleanup: drop old FK constraints and columns using online-safe DROP CONSTRAINT / DROP COLUMN - 2 days
Post-ops: VACUUM, ANALYZE, and update dashboards and runbook - 2 days
migration_strategy: Phased online approach: (1) add canonical tenant_id column if not present, (2) create new indexes CONCURRENTLY for hot queries to avoid planner regressions, (3) perform batched backfill from legacy columns with idempotent jobs and per-batch validation, (4) flip the read preference via a small feature flag rollout in the control plane, (5) after 72h of stable metrics and a successful canary, drop legacy FKs and columns. Use statement_timeouts and statement-level retries in backfills to avoid long-running locks.
rollback_plan: If data parity checks fail or latency regressions >10% persist in canary: (A) revert application read flag to legacy columns (fast rollback), (B) stop backfill jobs and resume later with lower throttle, (C) re-create dropped FK/column from backups if cleanup already started (follow DB restore runbook). We will keep a per-batch audit_log table (small, append-only) to allow replaying partial backfills if needed.
validation_queries:
-- Referential parity check (counts should match)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deployments d WHERE d.tenant_id IS DISTINCT FROM d.tenant_id_legacy;

-- Check for orphans after move
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM route_mappings r LEFT JOIN tenants t ON r.tenant_id = t.id WHERE t.id IS NULL;

-- Sample hash parity (fast)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT md5(id::text || '::' || tenant_id::text) h FROM api_keys) a JOIN (SELECT md5(id::text || '::' || tenant_id_legacy::text) h FROM api_keys) b USING (h);

-- Query plan comparison helper (run on staging)
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM route_mappings WHERE tenant_id = $1 AND status = 'active' LIMIT 100;
benchmarks: Baseline (staging): route resolution 95p = 210ms; expected after indexes = <=150ms
Backfill throughput target: 10k rows/min with <5% added CPU on primary during throttled windows
observability: Grafana: control-plane/sql-latency (added per-query tag for canonical vs legacy col)
SLO guardrails: alert if 95p for control-plane core endpoints increases by >10% during migration windows
Dashboards: index size, live progress of backfill (rows updated), and lock wait time
